result:
Unit 458 is complete: all five tasks (0 to 4) ran and none were dropped. 9.2 and 9.3 are ticked in both copies of `PHASE_PLAN.md`. Every commit is pushed, the last being `19109b51`. The full report is in `output.md` and passes the project's validator.

**What it found.** I scored both decoders on the same 23 keyed recordings and 12 synthetic cases through the same scoring calls. Across the whole corpus, fldigi's port reads worse than ours on all four metrics:

| condition | sure-character error, ours / port | coverage, ours / port | word-boundary errors, ours / port |
|---|---|---|---|
| real recordings (keys inferred, not transcribed) | 33 of 436 / 62 of 239 | 403 / 177 of 473 | 37 / 86 of 113 words |
| synthetic cases (keys exact) | 14 of 173 / 34 of 168 | 159 / 134 of 252 | 44 / 56 of 84 words |

- **Where the port wins:** it scores better on 13 of 35 recordings, on at least one metric. Six of those are only because it printed fewer characters. That includes the 0 dB synthetic cases, where it gets 2 characters right each time but gets most of the rest wrong.
- **Real reading differences:** in a few places ours lost dits or dahs that fldigi kept, and on one recording our speed estimate ran at 40 WPM against fldigi's 24.
- **How the port's output is scored:** every character it prints counts as sure, its no-match `*` counts as unreadable, and its spaces count as word breaks. That is the instruction's DECIDED (2), stated in `parity.md`.
- **Speed of output:** fldigi puts a character out about 0.30 s after the last mark, against about 1.27 s for ours. Spans are found by matching text, not by time, so this doesn't affect any score.

**Checks.** The self-check was seen failing first: a commit deliberately expected one wrong character too many (`01b6a651`), went red, then went green once corrected. Our decoder's row through the new test matches the existing metrics test exactly. Neither decoder changed: no source file moved, and every recording's text is identical to the start of the session. At exit every floor and metric was as at entry, and both carry-forward lines passed. The three named floors are still red at 38, 43 and 42, which is the known state.

**Things that will look odd:**
- **`parity.md` changes on every run.** Its decode-time rows are wall-clock times, so the file shows a small diff whenever the test runs. It's recorded in section 4 as housekeeping.
- **The app tests lost tests at entry.** Headless Avalonia's "dispatcher loop" error lost 3 tests, then 1 on the rerun. All four affected test groups passed when run alone. At exit the line passed 278 of 278 on the first run.

**Needs your call:**
- **How 9.3 was ticked.** I named fldigi's source lines for each of the 13 wins from the printed texts and evidence, not from a sample-by-sample trace. If you want traces, 9.3 goes back to open with all 13 printouts intact.
- **Still carried from unit 457:** the reading behind the 9.1 tick, which is waiting on your word.

`cw-2026-09-24-135641` isn't in the tree, so it wasn't run. The five captures ours reads as nothing were run through the port and printed unscored.
